in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Great! To get started, I need to understand your situation. Let me ask you some initial questions:

**1. Do you have a child or children you're claiming for?** If yes, could you tell me:
   - Their name(s)
   - Their age(s)

This will help me determine which eligibility path applies to your situation. Child Benefit eligibility depends on the age of the child and other factors we'll explore together.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm claiming for my son Alex. He's 19 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're claiming for your son Alex who is 19 years old.

Since Alex is between 16 and 19 years old, his eligibility depends on whether he's in approved education or training. Let me navigate to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now I need to understand Alex's current education or training situation:

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In approved education or training** (such as full-time non-advanced education at school, college, or an approved training program)?
2. **Recently left education or training** (within the last 20 weeks)?
3. **Neither** - not in education/training and didn't recently leave?

Could you let me know which situation applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure about that, to be honest. I don't know if what he's doing counts as approved education or training, or if he's recently left anything. I just know he's 19 and living with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
No problem! Let me help clarify this so we can determine what applies to Alex.

**For approved education or training, this typically includes:**

- **Full-time non-advanced education** at school or college (like A-levels, Scottish Highers, BTECs, NVQ Level 3 or below)
- **Approved training programs** (like traineeships or certain vocational courses)
- The education/training must be **full-time** (generally at least 12 hours per week of supervised study)

**It does NOT include:**
- University or higher education courses (degrees, HNDs)
- Part-time courses
- Apprenticeships
- Full-time paid work with some training attached

**So, to help figure this out, could you tell me:**

1. **Is Alex currently attending any school, college, or training program?**
2. **If yes, what type of course or program is it?** (e.g., A-levels, college course, training program, university degree, etc.)
3. **Is it full-time or part-time?**

Or if he's not in any education or training right now:
- **Did he leave or finish any education or training course recently?** If so, roughly when did that end?

This will help me determine which path applies to his situation!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I really don't know the answers to those questions. I can't tell you whether he's in education or training, what type it might be, or whether he's recently left anything. That's just not information I have right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I completely understand - you don't have that information available right now, and that's okay.

Unfortunately, to properly assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit, I do need to know his education or training status, as this is a critical factor for anyone aged 16-19. Without this information, I cannot definitively determine whether he qualifies as a "qualifying young person" under the Child Benefit rules.

**Here's what I can tell you:**

For a 19-year-old like Alex, Child Benefit eligibility depends on whether he:
- Is in approved full-time non-advanced education or training, OR
- Recently left education/training (within the last 20 weeks before his 20th birthday)

If neither of these applies, then unfortunately he would not qualify.

**What you can do:**

1. **Find out Alex's current status** - Ask him directly whether he's in any education or training program
2. **Contact the Child Benefit Office** - They can discuss your specific situation and help determine eligibility. You can call them at **0300 200 3100**
3. **Come back to me** once you have more information about Alex's education/training status, and I can complete the assessment

Would you like to find out this information and come back, or would you prefer I provide you with the contact details for the Child Benefit Office to discuss directly with them?

Based on what you've told me - that Alex is 19 and lives with you in the UK - I cannot determine eligibility because the rules for 16-19 year olds specifically require knowing their education or training status. This is a fundamental requirement in the Child Benefit legislation, not just a detail.

Since we cannot establish Alex's qualifying status with the information available, the outcome here is **INDETERMINATE** - meaning the rules cannot be fully applied without this critical information.

When you do contact them or gather more information about Alex's situation, you're welcome to come back and I can help assess eligibility again. Good luck!
